question: An 3-year-old boy is brought in to his pediatrician by his mother after she noticed that the child was starting to turn yellow. She has not noticed any behavioral changes. On exam, the boy is icteric but is behaving normally. His temperature is 98.8°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 108/78 mmHg, pulse is 78/min, and respirations are 14/min. His labs are drawn, and he is found to have an unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with a serum bilirubin of 15 mg/dL. The mother is counseled that this boy’s condition may require phenobarbital as a treatment to reduce his bilirubin levels. Which of the following is the most likely defect in this child?

options.opb: Defective liver excretion of bilirubin due to ABCC2 mutation
options.opc: Defective liver excretion of bilirubin due to SLCO1B1 and SLCO1B3 mutations

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Impaired bilirubin uptake -> unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia -> 80% CHAIN: Reduced UDP-glucuronosyltransferase activity -> decreased conjugation of bilirubin -> unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia -> 85% CHAIN: Absent UDP-glucuronosyltransferase activity -> decreased conjugation of bilirubin -> unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia -> 80% CHAIN: Defective liver excretion of bilirubin due to ABCC2 mutation -> unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia -> 70% CHAIN: Defective liver excretion of bilirubin due to SLCO1B1 and SLCO1B3 mutations -> unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia -> 80%
enhanced_information: The most likely defect in this child leading to unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia is reduced UDP-glucuronosyltransferase activity, which results in decreased conjugation of bilirubin. This aligns with the standard understanding of the condition. The evidence path confirming liver involvement in hyperbilirubinemia supports this conclusion.
